Run R Code as Tasks on Other Processes, Machines or a SLURM Cluster

Source: R/remoteComputing.R
distributedComputing.Rd

Saves the objects named in input, copies them with the code and the model files to the nodes given by on and runs the code there once per task, in the background. Returns functions to check, wait for, collect and delete the results. On Windows the local commands run in the sh of Rtools; remote nodes need a POSIX shell.

Usage

distributedComputing(
  expr,
  tasks = NULL,
  on = localNode(),
  jobname = NULL,
  input = ls(parent.frame()),
  build = c("auto", "compile", "link", "copy"),
  libs = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  wait = FALSE,
  recover = FALSE,
  buildCores = NULL,
  buildBundle = 50
)

Arguments

expr

R code, evaluated once per task.

tasks

A positive whole number of tasks, or a list or vector with one element per task, or a data frame with one row per task. NULL (default) is one task per worker.

on

Where the tasks run: localNode() (default), sshNodes() or slurmCluster().

jobname

Character, the name of the job and of the job folder. NULL (default) picks a random name.

input

Character vector, the objects saved and copied to the nodes, looked up from the calling environment. Defaults to all objects of the calling environment.

build

How the model files reach the nodes: "auto", "compile", "link" or "copy", see Details.

libs

Optional character vector of library paths put in front of the library search path on the nodes, for the tasks and the build. The remote shell expands them, so ~ is the remote home.

seed

Integer, task i starts with set.seed(seed + i). NULL (default) draws one.

wait

Logical. TRUE waits for the tasks, returns the results of get() and deletes the job with purge(local = TRUE); a job with failed tasks is kept. Default FALSE.

recover

Logical. TRUE returns the functions of the job jobname, submitted from this working directory or registered, without submitting again. Else, with on given, the manifest is taken from the job folder of the remote nodes, which recovers a job submitted from another machine; it is then saved in <jobname>_folder of the working directory and registered. A job that also runs on "localhost" is recovered only on the machine it was submitted from. Default FALSE.

buildCores

Number of parallel compiler processes of a build. NULL (default) uses the cores the node reports, at most 16.

buildBundle

Number of generated sources a build puts into one translation unit, only for builds with more files than the shell accepts as arguments. 1 compiles one file at a time. Default 50.

Value

With wait = TRUE the results of get(), else an object of class dMod2Job, a list of functions:

check()

reports how many tasks are done, running, failed or not reachable and returns TRUE once no task runs or is not reachable, with a warning when some failed. A task fails when the task process ends without a result. A task without a result on a node that does not answer, or whose queue does not, is not reachable.

wait(interval = 10)

polls every interval seconds until no task runs or is not reachable, reports each change as a message and returns TRUE when every task is done. While a node does not answer, the pause between polls doubles up to 10 minutes.

get(combine = TRUE, all = FALSE)

returns the results. With combine = TRUE parlists are joined by c(), fits of msem() that each ran a part of the same starts into one fit, and data frames such as parframes by rbind(), other results come as a list; tasks without a result are left out with a warning. combine = FALSE returns one entry per task, named like tasks, NULL for a task not done. Results of remote nodes are copied into <jobname>_folder/<k>, with all = TRUE together with every other file of the job folder.

log(i, lines = 20)

prints the last lines of the output of task i.

purge(local = FALSE)

deletes the job folders on the nodes, with local = TRUE also the local <jobname>_folder and the registry entry.

terminate()

stops the tasks.

Details

The start is reported as a message, on a SLURM cluster with the job ID. A build writes the output to build.log in the job folder; the error of a failed build shows the end of that log.

The value of expr is the result of a task. In the code, task is the task's element of tasks (NULL for a count), taskId the position of the task, cores the cores the task may use and jobname the job's name. Parallel code such as mstrust() or profile() takes cores = cores. A task that raises an error returns the error as a try-error. Task i starts with the seed seed + i.

The tasks are dealt in turn to the workers of on, the nodes or the array tasks of a SLURM job, and a worker runs the tasks dealt to it one after the other, see localNode(). A job is kept in <jobname>_folder, in the working directory for "localhost" and in the home directory of a remote node. The job manifest job.rds lies in the local <jobname>_folder and in that of every remote node. A job of the same name that still runs there is an error, also when it was submitted from another machine, and so is a job of the same name in the folder of a remote node that was submitted from another working directory, until it is purged. Every job is registered in tools::R_user_dir("dMod2", "data") until purge(local = TRUE), and dMod2Jobs() lists them.

The model files are those of the obsfn, parfn, prdfn and objective objects in input; when none of them has model files, those in getOption("dMod2.outdir"), else in the working directory.

  • build = "compile": the C/C++ sources are copied and compiled once per node into one shared object, against the cppDE installed there.

  • build = "link": the object files (.o) are copied and linked once per node; needs a compiler there compatible with the local one.

  • build = "copy": the shared objects are copied.

  • build = "auto" (default): "copy" on the local machine, "compile" elsewhere.

After a build the obsfn, parfn and prdfn objects and the objectives use the new shared object.

See also

localNode(), slurmTemplate(), dMod2Jobs(), detectFreeCores(); the guide chapter Remote computing.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Two tasks on the local machine, in a temporary working directory; each task
# starts an R process
if (.Platform$OS.type == "unix") {
  old <- setwd(tempdir())
  M <- matrix(rnorm(1e2), 10, 10)
  job <- distributedComputing(det(M * task), tasks = list(a = 1, b = 2),
                              input = "M", jobname = "example")
  job$wait(interval = 0.1)
  print(job$get())
  job$purge(local = TRUE)
  setwd(old)
}
#> example: 2 tasks started on localhost (3 cores)
#> example: 0 of 2 tasks done, 2 running
#> example: 1 of 2 tasks done, 1 running
#> example: 2 of 2 tasks done
#> $a
#> [1] -403.4075
#> 
#> $b
#> [1] -413089.3
#> 
# }

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# For an objective obj and a center of the starts: multistarts on two nodes
# reached by ssh, one task per node with ten fits per core
nodes <- sshNodes(c("server1", "server2"), cores = 16)
jobFitting <- distributedComputing(
  mstrust(obj, center, fits = 10 * cores, cores = cores, sd = 4),
  on = nodes, jobname = "fits"
)
jobFitting$wait()
bestfit <- as.parvec(jobFitting$get())
jobFitting$purge(local = TRUE)

# Profiles of the best fit: one task per group of four parameters and side, on
# the free cores of both nodes. get() joins the sides of every parameter.
groups <- split(names(bestfit), ceiling(seq_along(bestfit) / 4))
jobProfiling <- distributedComputing(
  profile(obj, bestfit, whichPar = groups[[task$group]], side = task$side,
          limits = c(-5, 5), cores = cores),
  tasks = expand.grid(group = seq_along(groups), side = c("left", "right"),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  on = sshNodes(c("server1", "server2")), jobname = "profiles"
)
jobProfiling$wait()
profiles <- jobProfiling$get()
confint(profiles)

# 1000 fits on a SLURM cluster: 100 array tasks of 10 fits on 10 cores each,
# through the job script template of the login node "mycluster", set up once
# from a job script of the cluster with the placeholders of ?slurmTemplate.
slurmTemplate("mycluster", from = "~/mycluster.sh")
cluster <- slurmCluster("mycluster", cores = 10, walltime = "02:00:00")
job <- distributedComputing(
  mstrust(obj, center, fits = cores, cores = cores, sd = 4),
  tasks = 100, on = cluster, jobname = "slurmfits"
)

# The ten starts of one mixed-effects multistart as ten array tasks of four cores:
# every task draws the same starts and fits a separate part, get() joins them into one fit
jobEm <- distributedComputing({
  set.seed(1)
  msem(obj, random, init, fits = 10, which = taskId,
       cores = c(fits = 1, conditions = cores))
}, tasks = 10, on = slurmCluster("mycluster", cores = 4, walltime = "06:00:00"),
jobname = "msemfits")

# The jobs submitted and not purged, and the functions of one of them
dMod2Jobs()
job <- distributedComputing(NULL, jobname = "slurmfits", recover = TRUE)
} # }
